• Draw the block diagram and give short explanation
  • LDI R16,0x00 ; Clear R16 (will hold the LOW byte of the product)
  • LDI R17,0x00 ; Clear R17 (will hold the HIGH byte of the product)
  • LDS R0,0x60 ; Load first operand (multiplicand) from SRAM address 0x60
  • LDS R1,0x61 ; Load second operand (multiplier) from SRAM address 0x61
  • L2: ADD R16,R0 ; Add multiplicand (R0) to result low byte (R16)
  • BRCC L1 ; If no carry from ADD, skip increment of high byte
  • INC R17 ; If carry occurred, increment high byte (R17)
  • L1: DEC R1 ; Decrement multiplier (R1)
  • BRNE L2 ; Repeat loop until multiplier reaches zero

questions.question: Explain the features of embedded C. Describe the basic structure of a AVR C program, with a suitable example
questions.solution_html:
• Ease of Programming
  • C is easier to learn and use than assembly language, while still
  • providing the necessary control over hardware.
  • Easy to modify and update
  • Low-Level Access
  • C allows direct manipulation of hardware registers and peripherals
  • which is essential for embedded systems programming.
  • Portability
  • Code written in C can be easily ported to different AVR devices and
  • even other microcontroller families, with minimal modifications.
  • Efficiency
  • C compilers can generate efficient machine code for AVRs, enabling
  • fast execution and optimal resource utilization.
  • Community Support
  • AVR microcontrollers have a large and active community, providing
  • ample resources, libraries, and support for C programming.
  • Wide Range of Applications
  • AVR microcontrollers are used in diverse applications, including IoT
  • devices, home automation, robotics, and industrial automation, all of
  • which often rely on Embedded C for their functionality.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: &Explain the basic structure with suitable embedded C program
